newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS / PepsiCo calls.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS / PepsiCo calls.

text.p: Out-of-the-money call options in PepsiCo Inc continued to see heavy order flows amid vague rumors that the firm could be a target of acquisition, traders said.
"There's rumor out there that Philip Morris (Cos Inc) is looking at this company," said a trader in the Pepsico pit at the Chicago Board Options Exchange (CBOE).
Pepsi November 30 and 32.5 calls had turnover of 3,803 and 1,913 contracts by mid-afternoon. Time-and-sale figures showed much of the orders came in relatively small blocks.

The November 30 call had volume of 7,276 contracts on Wednesday. While part of the volume was due to roll-over from Octobers, which expire at the end of the week, it pushed up open interest by 3,976 contracts to 6173 as of end-Wednesday.
PepsiCo stock was the busiest stock on the New York Stock Exchange, with the price gaining 1 to 30-1/8 on volume of 7,837,200.

"It broke through the 30-strike pretty straight, and when this happened it created a lot of interest," said a second CBOE floor trader. He declined to say if he thought the takeover rumor was credible.
Still, most traders doubted such a deal would take place, noting that option prices showed little sign of aggressive bidding by someone strongly convinced of a buyout.
Implied volatility for November 30 call, for instance, stood at about 30 percent, barely above the stock's historical volatility, said Harrison Roth, first vice president of Cowen & Co.
"That's a story, but I don't believe it," Roth said of the rumor.
Officials from PepsiCo and Philip Morris declined to comment on the rumor, citing company policy.

Marty Kearney at PTI Securities said some major brokerage firms had reiterated their buy ratings on Pepsico recently, despite PepsiCo's dismal third quarter earnings results released earlier in the week.
"Nobody's saying anything great, other than that the bad news is behind them," he added, however.
PepsiCo's earnings came in at $0.09 per share after charges, compared with $0.39 a year earlier.
